demo.META_DESCRIPTION: Try live FastComments demos including commenting widgets, ratings, SSO, anonymous commenting, badges, dark mode, WYSIWYG editor, and more.
demo.HERO_DESCRIPTION: FastComments is packed with features, but don't let that fool you. With every release we've kept the our commenting product free of bloat. Try out the live demo below.
demo.DEMO_SELECTOR_SUBTITLE: FastComments supports many different use cases. Try one below!
demo.OUR_CUSTOMERS_SUBTEXT: No Credit Card Required For Initial Sign up & Installation
demo.DEMO_OPTION_RATINGS_ABOUT: Here we have two widgets. The summary widget, and the commenting widget. We've added some questions in the dashboard under Customize->Questions and added a widget configuration under Customize->Customize which uses our questions. We've setup the widget configuration to only apply to this page, as well, but you could setup questions to show on all pages or a specific subdomain.
demo.DEMO_OPTION_SSO_ABOUT:
Here we're using the FastComment Secure SSO solution. This makes an API call when you select the button to get the user's information which is hashed against an API with an SHA-256 hash for verification. The code is very similar to this.

FastComments also supports what we call Simple SSO, which doesn't require a server.

With both solutions we can configure if the user is a moderator, an admin, add custom labels, badges, notification preferences, etc.
demo.DEMO_OPTION_ANON_ABOUT: In this example we've turned on a few settings. We enabled anonymous commenting, but this alone would still show the email input field and just make it optional. We've also hidden the email input field and allowed anonymous voting and flagging. This was all configured via the admin dashboard, no code written.
demo.DEMO_OPTION_BADGES_ABOUT:
FastComments supports what we call badges, which are awarded to users automatically based on various conditions. There are three badges you can earn here:
  • Curious: Awarded for commenting on this page.
  • Very Curious: Awarded for commenting on this page more than once. Configured to replace the Curious badge.
  • Night Owl: Awarded for commenting on this page at night.
  • Well Liked: Awarded when you receive 5 or more total karma on this page.
These will automatically be applied to your account and shown. You can hide them by going to you profile (click your avatar) and clicking the three-dot menu and clicking Manage Badges. This will only work in a fully authenticated verified session and not an anon session.
demo.DEMO_OPTION_DARK_MODE_ABOUT:
In this example we turn on dark mode for the whole page. The commenting widget automatically detects the DOM tree it is in contains a dark background and adjusts.

You can use an API to configure this behavior as well.
demo.DEMO_OPTION_LIKES_DESC: Use likes instead of up/down votes.
demo.DEMO_OPTION_CODE_SNIPPETS_DESC: FastComments supports dev communities by auto-detecting code snippet languages and formatting them.
demo.DEMO_OPTION_CODE_SNIPPETS_ABOUT:
Some communities, for example Stack Overflow, promote sharing of code between developers. FastComments is designed to fit in these communities by gracefully handling code snippets while sanitizing content to prevent against XSS or style attacks.
You can learn more about the security of the comment area here.
demo.DEMO_OPTION_WYSIWYG_DESC: Rich text editor for easier commenting.
demo.DEMO_OPTION_WYSIWYG_ABOUT:
The WYSIWYG (What You See Is What You Get) editor provides a rich text editing experience for users who prefer visual formatting over markdown. It includes common formatting options like bold, italic, links, and lists while maintaining the security and performance standards of FastComments.

This is particularly useful for non-technical communities where users might not be familiar with markdown syntax. This example also enables the resize handle.
demo.DEMO_OPTION_TOS_ABOUT:
This demo shows the Terms of Service checkbox that can be required for first-time commenters. When enabled, anonymous users see the checkbox on every comment, while authenticated users only see it on their first comment or when you update your TOS.

You can customize the checkbox text per locale and set a "Last Updated" date to force users to re-accept when your terms change.
demo.DEMO_OPTION_AI_AGENTS_ABOUT: This is a demo of our AI Agents feature. An agent is configured to periodically summarize the comments and leave a comment and pin it. Additionally, another agent is configured to send you a welcome email the first time you comment here (if you haven't commented on any of our other demos yet). An AI agent is also configured to do general moderation.
demo.DEMO_OPTION_AI_AGENTS_DESC: Thread summarization using AI Agents, along with some other AI Agent features like welcome emails.
demo.DEMO_OPTION_USER_LIST_DESC: Show a sidebar of online viewers and past commenters next to the widget.
demo.DEMO_OPTION_USER_LIST_ABOUT: Renders a list of people on this page beside the comment widget. The Online Participants section shows everyone currently viewing in real time; the Offline Participants section lists past commenters when usersListIncludeOffline is enabled. Configurable to render as a top facepile, a left sidebar, or a right sidebar.

marketing_common.FAQ_CAN_MIGRATE: Can I migrate my data from my existing solution?
marketing_common.FAQ_CAN_MIGRATE_ANSWER: All plans support automated self-service migration from a selection of major providers. We perform custom migrations.
marketing_common.FAQ_CUSTOMIZE_UI: Can we customize the UI of the comment widget?
marketing_common.FAQ_CUSTOMIZE_UI_ANSWER: Yes, the comment widget is designed to be customized.
marketing_common.FAQ_EXISTING_ACCOUNTS: What if my users already have accounts? They have to have an account to comment now too?
marketing_common.FAQ_EXISTING_ACCOUNTS_ANSWER: FastComments supports SSO, which means that your users can have one login for your site/application, and commenting.
marketing_common.FAQ_REQUIREMENTS: Does FastComments require anything special on my site to run?
marketing_common.FAQ_REQUIREMENTS_ANSWER: No, our commenting widget has no dependencies.
marketing_common.FAQ_CUSTOMER_SERVICE_SLAS: What are your customer service SLAs?
marketing_common.FAQ_CUSTOMER_SERVICE_SLAS_ANSWER: We generally respond within an hour during business hours, and 24 hours at most. There is a ticketing system within the admin area.
marketing_common.FAQ_CANCEL_MYSELF_ANSWER: You can cancel without any intervention from customer support, although we'll reach out to hear what we could have done better!
marketing_common.FAQ_TRIAL_ENDS: What happens when the trial ends?
marketing_common.FAQ_TRIAL_ENDS_ANSWER: The comment widget will still function for a short time, and then hide itself. You and your users will still have full access to the admin area. You will receive reminders, which you can easily opt out of, when the trial ends.
marketing_common.FAQ_EXCEED_LIMITS: What if I exceed the limits of my account?
marketing_common.FAQ_EXCEED_LIMITS_ANSWER: All package details, except for number of comments per month, are hard limits. If you exceed the number of comments per month, we'll reach out to you to negotiate your package. On the Flex plan, you set your own limits from the Billing page to cap your monthly spend.
marketing_common.FAQ_FREE_TIER: I run an open source project with low traffic, is there a free tier?
marketing_common.FAQ_FREE_TIER_ANSWER: There is currently no official free tier, however for example adding comments to OSS documentation pages we make exceptions. Simply create a support ticket after signing up.
marketing_common.FAQ_ADD_USERS: Can I add my developers, moderators, and other admins?
marketing_common.FAQ_ADD_USERS_ANSWER: Yes, FastComments supports adding other users to your account and controlling their permissions.
marketing_common.FAQ_COOKIE_BANNER: Do I need to add a cookie banner to my site?
marketing_common.FAQ_COOKIE_BANNER_ANSWER: You are not required to add a cookie banner on your site if you use FastComments. We only add functional cookies for logging in, and do not add any tracking cookies or cookies that would personally identify your user, to your site.
marketing_common.FAQ_COMMENT_BOX_LIMIT: Is there a limit on the number of comment boxes I can have?
marketing_common.FAQ_COMMENT_BOX_LIMIT_ANSWER: FastComments does not bill on the number of comment boxes, or threads, that you may have. There is no limit today, either. We instead bill on traffic and comment volume.
marketing_common.FAQ_SEO_INDEXABLE: Are comments indexable via search engines?
marketing_common.FAQ_SEO_INDEXABLE_ANSWER: Yes, we ensure that comment threads can be indexed by search engines. Learn more
marketing_common.FAQ_ALL_WIDGETS: Do I get access to all widgets on all places?
marketing_common.FAQ_ALL_WIDGETS_ANSWER: Yes. All plans include all widgets (live commenting, live chat, small widgets, etc).
marketing_common.FAQ_DATA_STORAGE: What countries is my data stored?
marketing_common.FAQ_DATA_STORAGE_ANSWER:
We have different deployments for different use cases. By default, FastComments globally replicates all data to many continents.

We do not have any servers in China. We have a node in Singapore for our customers in that region.

For our EU customers, if your account resides on eu.fastcomments.com, data stays in the EU.
marketing_common.FAQ_BILLING_SCHEDULE: What is the billing schedule for Flex?
marketing_common.FAQ_BILLING_SCHEDULE_ANSWER: You are billed at the end of every month based on your usage, not on the signup date.
marketing_common.FAQ_PAY_YEARLY_ANSWER: You can pay yearly for the non-flex billing plans.
marketing_common.FAQ_CHARGE_MODERATORS: So you charge based on how many moderators and admins I have?
marketing_common.FAQ_CHARGE_MODERATORS_ANSWER: Yes, to make pricing easier for small and large companies, we pay for admin and moderator seats. We usually offer bulk pricing for very large organizations.
marketing_common.FAQ_TWO_SITES: What if I have two sites, how am I billed?
marketing_common.FAQ_TWO_SITES_ANSWER: Some packages like the Creators plan include up to 3 sites. The Flex plan gives you the first one free, so with two sites you'd pay a total of $10/mo, but it also includes de-branding which Creators does not.
marketing_common.FAQ_SUBDOMAIN: What if I have mysite.com and subdomain.mysite.com?
marketing_common.FAQ_SUBDOMAIN_ANSWER: This depends on the setup. If you add mysite.com to your account, it would be billed as one, and the data/comments are still stored separately. However, let's say you want specific configuration for subdomain.mysite.com - then you'd have to add it separately in your account and it'd be billed as such.
marketing_common.FAQ_MISSED_PAYMENT_ANSWER: The system gives you a grace period of a week to pay unpaid invoices, and then your account will be paused. Unpaid accounts are deleted after a year.
marketing_common.PUBLIC_NAV_ITEM_AI_AGENTS_DESC: Moderation that shows its work. Dry-run, audited, capped.
marketing_common.PUBLIC_NAV_ITEM_WEBFLOW_DESC: Add comments from the Webflow Designer.
marketing_common.PUBLIC_NAV_ITEM_COMMENTING_API_DESC: REST API and SDKs for live discussions.
marketing_common.FAQ_FLEX_SPEND_LIMIT: Can I set a spending limit on Flex?
marketing_common.FAQ_FLEX_SPEND_LIMIT_ANSWER: Yes. On the Billing page in your dashboard, enter a target monthly maximum and we'll set the matching usage limits for you, or fine-tune each limit yourself. Usage that would exceed a limit is blocked, which caps what you're billed.

my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_CUSTOMIZE_INTRO_1: You've come to the right place if you want to make FastComments look like your own.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_CUSTOMIZE_INTRO_2: These settings will affect how FastComments looks on your site. You can define these customizations as "rules" - a rule can apply to a whole domain or a single page.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.HEADING_WHAT_SITE_TO_CUSTOMIZE: What site do you want to customize?
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_DOMAIN_NOTE: This is optional. Select All Domains and the rules will apply to all sites. Don't see your site listed? Add it here.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_URL_ID_NOTE_1: This is optional. Leave it blank or enter * and the rules will apply to all pages.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_URL_ID_NOTE_2: Patterns are also supported! For example you could have */blog/* in one configuration and */store/* in another.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.OPTION_AUTOMATIC: Automatic (detect light or dark site background)
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_AUTOMATIC_NOTE: Automatic styling will detect your site's color scheme and attempt to match it. If the site is dark, we'll enable dark mode, for example.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_FORCE_DARK_NOTE: Force Dark Mode will mean your site must have a dark background, otherwise text may be unreadable.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_FORCE_WRAPPED_NOTE: Force Wrapped will put the comment widget in a container with a white background to isolate it from your site.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_NEVER_WRAP_NOTE: Never Wrap is like Auto but only Dark Mode. We'll never put the widget in a container with its own background.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_COMMENT_COUNT_FORMAT_NOTE: Use [count] to represent the localized comment count.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_HIDE_AVATARS_NOTE: Even if someone has an avatar, it won't show next to their name.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_GIF_RATING_NOTE: When image uploads are allowed, this controls the rating of gifs shown in the Gif Picker.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_IMAGE_PROFANITY_NOTE: Controls the level of profanity moderation for uploaded images.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_PROFANITY_LOW: Low: Blocks explicit sexual and violence content
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_PROFANITY_MEDIUM: Medium: Also blocks hate, harassment and self-harm content
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_DISABLE_BLOCKING_NOTE: Do not allow users to block other users. Does not affect existing blocked users.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.LABEL_INPUT_AFTER_COMMENTS: Move reply box to the bottom of the page?
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_INPUT_AFTER_COMMENTS_NOTE: Want people to read the comments before replying?
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_CLICK_TO_SHOW_COMMENTS_NOTE: Hide the comment list and the comment box under a link?
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_USE_SHOW_COMMENTS_TOGGLE_NOTE: Click to show comments, with the ability to show a number of comments by default. Shows the comment box by default.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_COUNT_ABOVE_TOGGLE_NOTE: How many comments should we show above the "Show Comments" button?
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_PREVENT_NEW_REPLIES_NOTE: Enabling this will disable commenting, but show previous comments, for the defined site/url.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_PREVENT_NEW_ROOT_COMMENTS_NOTE: Enabling this will disable creating new top-level comments, but allow replying to existing comments.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_COLLAPSE_LIVE_COMMENTS_NOTE: Enabling this will collapse "live" comments under a "Show X New Comments" button. Otherwise, new live comments will show normally as they are added.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_DISABLE_LIVE_COMMENTING_NOTE: Enabling this will turn off all live features. Clients will not show live updates to the comment feed, votes, comment changes (edits, deletes), and result of moderation actions.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.LABEL_REQUIRE_SSO: Require SSO To View Comments
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_REQUIRE_SSO_NOTE: Enabling this will require commenters to be logged in via SSO (single-sign-on) to view the comment widget. Does not apply to the site admin.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_SSO_SECURITY_LEVEL_NOTE: Choose Simple SSO for third party integrations, Secure SSO for custom server-based integrations.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.LABEL_LIMIT_COMMENTS_BY_GROUPS: Limit Comments by SSO User Groups
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_LIMIT_COMMENTS_BY_GROUPS_NOTE: With this enabled, users will only see comments from their same access groups.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_ENABLE_COMMENTER_LINKS_NOTE: Enabling this will show a field for entering a website or blog URL when commenting. The commenter's username then links to this URL.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_SINGLE_LINE_COMMENT_INPUT_NOTE: Enabling this will change the multi-line comment input field into a single-row input.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.LABEL_COLLAPSE_REPLIES: Collapse Replies to Top-Level Comments by Default
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_COLLAPSE_REPLIES_NOTE: Enabling this will require users to click "Show Replies" to see child comments.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_ENABLE_WYSIWYG_NOTE: Enables WYSIWYG editing which allows formatting text without using visible anchor tags.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_ENABLE_RESIZE_HANDLE_NOTE: Allows users to resize comment input areas by dragging the corner.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_ENABLE_SPOILERS_NOTE: Adds a "SPOILER" button to the editor toolbar.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_DISABLE_TOOLBAR_NOTE: The comment reply toolbar, commonly called a WYSIWYG toolbar, will not show. Users will not be able to make text bold, for example, or upload images.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_DISABLE_VOTING_NOTE: Users will not be able to vote, and existing vote counts will be hidden.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_VOTE_STYLE_NOTE: When the heart icon is enabled, down voting is not possible and also validated server-side.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_ENABLE_VOTE_LIST_NOTE: Show users' names when hovering over comment vote counts.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_DISABLE_COMMENTER_COMMENT_DELETE_NO: Commenters will not be able to delete their comments.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_DISABLE_COMMENTER_COMMENT_EDIT_NOTE: Commenters will not be able to edit their comments.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_DISABLE_AUTO_HASHTAG_CREATION_NOTE: New hash tags will not be automatically bolded. A list of hash tags will have to be provided instead, to enable hash tags. The list of tags can also be maintained via the API.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_DISABLE_NOTIFICATION_BELL_NOTE: The notification bell tells users when someone has replied to them, or replied in a thread they are active in, and more. It can also be used to subscribe to a page.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_DISABLE_PROFILES_NOTE: Disables opening the user's profile when you click on their avatar.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_SHOW_BADGES_IN_TOP_BAR_NOTE: Shows user badges next to their username in the comment reply top bar.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_DEFAULT_SORT_DIRECTION_NOTE: This will set the default sort direction of the comments. Users can still change it after the comments load.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_LOCALE_OVERRIDE_NOTE: This will set the locale for the comment widget, no matter what the user's browser is set to.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.TEXT_PAGE_SIZE_NOTE: This will set the number of comments per-page. Upon changing, it may take several minutes to update all comment threads.
my-account-customize-widget-edit.OPTION_NAME_FORMAT_CAPITALIZE: Capitalize (display example user as Example User)

my-account-manage-data-import-scheduled-.HEADING: Schedule Comments
my-account-manage-data-import-scheduled-.DESCRIPTION_PART1: Here you can schedule comments to be automatically posted, live, over time. This can allow you to annotate pages, like webinars, or even kick off discussion on a page for a live event in an automated way.
my-account-manage-data-import-scheduled-.DESCRIPTION_PART2: This is done by importing comments using the supported CSV Format (example here).
my-account-manage-data-import-scheduled-.DESCRIPTION_SCHEDULING_TYPES: There are two types of scheduling. The first is that the comments start playing on every page load, which is when "Every Page Load" is selected, and the second type is manually scheduling the comments by coming here and clicking "start".
my-account-manage-data-import-scheduled-.AUTO_PLAY_WARNING: Note! Adding Auto-Play comments (by selecting "Every Page Load" below) will cause any new comments posted in an autoplay thread to be added to the autoplay script. The comments can be moderated via the Moderate Comments page.

my-account-manage-data-webhooks.HEADING: Webhooks
my-account-manage-data-webhooks.PRODUCTION_NOTE_1: Ensure that you verify the "token" parameter in the request. This will be populated with your API secret, available here.
my-account-manage-data-webhooks.PRODUCTION_NOTE_2: When an invalid token is provided, return 401 Unauthorized.
my-account-manage-data-webhooks.PRODUCTION_NOTE_3: When a valid token is provided, return 200 OK.
my-account-manage-data-webhooks.PRODUCTION_NOTE_4: Not doing so will cause the integration to fail validation.
my-account-manage-data-webhooks.PRODUCTION_NOTE_5: Note that events are not immediate. There may be up to a minute delay as our system is asynchronous.
my-account-manage-data-webhooks.PRODUCTION_NOTE_6: If you do not return a 200 OK status code we will try again after minute. The delay increases by a minute after each failure for that event.
my-account-manage-data-webhooks.DOCUMENTATION_LINK_TEXT: For documentation and the request structure, see here.

my-account-managed-tenants-create.HEADING: Create a Managed Tenant
my-account-managed-tenants-create.INTRO_PARAGRAPH_1: Creating a managed tenant allows you to manage the tenant from your parent account. This is useful for reselling FastComments, or providing isolated accounts to your clients.
my-account-managed-tenants-create.INTRO_PARAGRAPH_2: You don't need to do this to use FastComments. However, if you want to have multiple sites and completely isolate each site with its own moderators and users, it can be useful to have them as their own tenants.
my-account-managed-tenants-create.WEBSITE_ADDRESS_HEADING: What is the address of the website where FastComments will show for this tenant?
my-account-managed-tenants-create.WEBSITE_ADDRESS_DESCRIPTION: No need to input subdomains or localhost. For multiple sites, separate them with commas.
my-account-managed-tenants-create.LIMITS_AND_PRICING_DESCRIPTION: With FastComments, you can customize the available packages to the tenant on a per-tenant basis. The below is populated by default with the limits and pricing of this parent tenant. Currently, you must bill your customer outside of FastComments. We will bill you based on their usage if you are on a Flex plan, or a flat rate on the Pro plan. You can find the pricing for this here.
my-account-managed-tenants-create.USAGE_LIMITS_DESCRIPTION: Limits are limited to the values of the current tenant. You may raise these by working with support. You may want to lower these values to limit what the managed tenant can do.

my-account-moderate-comments-banned-user.HEADING: Banned Users
my-account-moderate-comments-banned-user.INTRO_PARAGRAPH_1: Below is a list of your users, or emails, that have been banned from commenting or voting on your domains. If a user is "shadow banned" their comments and votes will still appear to post for them, but they won't be saved.
my-account-moderate-comments-banned-user.INTRO_PARAGRAPH_2: You can ban users via the "ban" option on the Moderate Comments page, or by clicking the plus icon at the bottom of this page if you have a specific email to ban.
my-account-moderate-comments-banned-user.INTRO_PARAGRAPH_3: When banned users try to comment it will show up in the audit log with the description "Banned user blocked from commenting."
my-account-moderate-comments-banned-user.IP_BAN_WARNING: FastComments does not store raw IP addresses for IP based banning. Be careful when using IP based bans as IP addresses can be reassigned.

Shadow banning will make it appear as their votes or comments are successful, but they won't persist.

my-account-moderate-comments-settings.HEADING: Comment Moderation Settings
my-account-moderate-comments-settings.ENABLE_PROFANITY_DETECTION_DESCRIPTION: Comments are checked for profanity in real-time. Does not affect comments by administrators or moderators.
my-account-moderate-comments-settings.AUTO_SEND_PROFANE_TO_SPAM_LABEL: Automatically Send Profane Comments to Spam
my-account-moderate-comments-settings.AUTO_SEND_PROFANE_TO_SPAM_DESCRIPTION: Instead of being masked, profane comments (determined via the phrase blacklist) will be hidden and marked as spam.
my-account-moderate-comments-settings.ALLOW_PROFANE_NAMES_DESCRIPTION: When enabled, commenter names will not be checked for profanity or masked.
my-account-moderate-comments-settings.ENABLE_SPAM_DETECTION_DESCRIPTION: Spam detection happens in real-time. Comments that look like spam will be hidden. Moderators can review and approve them as needed. Admins and moderator comments are excluded.
my-account-moderate-comments-settings.BLOCK_SPAM_DESCRIPTION: Instead of allowing comments that look like spam, and approving them later, block them and tell the user to change their comment. The comments will not be submitted for moderation. For sites where the spam volume is too high to moderate.
my-account-moderate-comments-settings.SPAM_FILTER_DESCRIPTION_BAYES: With Naïve Bayes, you can use the spam filter everyone else uses, or isolate your spam filter training to just your tenant. Both continuously learn.
my-account-moderate-comments-settings.SPAM_FILTER_DESCRIPTION_LLM_AVAILABLE: Select an LLM option for AI-powered spam detection (billed $<%= (tenantPackage.flexLLMCostCents * 10000 / tenantPackage.flexLLMUnit).toFixed(2) %> per 1M tokens). Only non-obvious spam is sent to the LLM to reduce costs.
my-account-moderate-comments-settings.SPAM_FILTER_DESCRIPTION_LLM_UNAVAILABLE: LLM-based spam detection is available for Flex (custom packages available).
my-account-moderate-comments-settings.AUTO_APPROVE_COMMENTS_DESCRIPTION: Changing this setting will not affect past comments.

product-demo-collab-chat.META_DESCRIPTION: Try the FastComments Collab Chat demo. Add inline discussions and text annotations to any content on your website or application.
product-demo-collab-chat.DESCRIPTION: Add discussions to any text content. Create interactive annotations on your content.
product-demo-collab-chat.MESSAGE_INTRO_1: FastComments Collab Chat provides users with the ability to create a discussion and annotate any piece of text. Simply highlight a few words, or paragraph, and start a discussion.
product-demo-collab-chat.MESSAGE_INTRO_2: You also might want to checkout Collab Chat in use by Govscent.org!
product-demo-collab-chat.TEXT_SOLAR_1: The Solar System is the gravitationally bound system of the Sun and the objects that orbit it. It formed 4.6 billion years ago from the gravitational collapse of a giant interstellar molecular cloud. The vast majority (99.86%) of the system's mass is in the Sun, with most of the remaining mass contained in the planet Jupiter. The planetary system around the Sun contains eight planets. The four inner system planets—Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars—are terrestrial planets, being composed primarily of rock and metal. The four giant planets of the outer system are substantially larger and more massive than the terrestrials. The two largest, Jupiter and Saturn, are gas giants, being composed mainly of hydrogen and helium; the next two, Uranus and Neptune, are ice giants, being composed mostly of volatile substances with relatively high melting points compared with hydrogen and helium, such as water, ammonia, and methane. All eight planets have nearly circular orbits that lie near the plane of Earth's orbit, called the ecliptic.
product-demo-collab-chat.TEXT_SOLAR_2: There are an unknown number of smaller dwarf planets and innumerable small Solar System bodies orbiting the Sun. Six of the major planets, the six largest possible dwarf planets, and many of the smaller bodies are orbited by natural satellites, commonly called "moons" after Earth's Moon. Two natural satellites, Jupiter's moon Ganymede and Saturn's moon Titan, are larger than Mercury, the smallest terrestrial planet, though less massive, and Jupiter's moon Callisto is nearly as large. Each of the giant planets and some smaller bodies are encircled by planetary rings of ice, dust and moonlets. The asteroid belt, which lies between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter, contains objects composed of rock, metal and ice. Beyond Neptune's orbit lie the Kuiper belt and scattered disc, which are populations of objects composed mostly of ice and rock.
product-demo-collab-chat.TEXT_SOLAR_3: In the outer reaches of the Solar System lies a class of minor planets called detached objects. There is considerable debate as to how many such objects there will prove to be. Some of these objects are large enough to have rounded under their own gravity and thus to be categorized as dwarf planets. Astronomers generally accept about nine objects as dwarf planets: the asteroid Ceres, the Kuiper-belt objects Pluto, Orcus, Haumea, Quaoar, and Makemake, and the scattered-disc objects Gonggong, Eris, and Sedna. Various small-body populations, including comets, centaurs and interplanetary dust clouds, freely travel between the regions of the Solar System.
product-demo-collab-chat.TEXT_SOLAR_4: The solar wind, a stream of charged particles flowing outwards from the Sun, creates a bubble-like region of interplanetary medium in the interstellar medium known as the heliosphere. The heliopause is the point at which pressure from the solar wind is equal to the opposing pressure of the interstellar medium; it extends out to the edge of the scattered disc. The Oort cloud, which is thought to be the source for long-period comets, may also exist at a distance roughly a thousand times further than the heliosphere. The Solar System is located 26,000 light-years from the center of the Milky Way galaxy in the Orion Arm, which contains most of the visible stars in the night sky. The nearest stars are within the so-called Local Bubble, with the closest, Proxima Centauri, at 4.2441 light-years.
product-demo-collab-chat.TEXT_STRUCTURE_1: The word solar means "pertaining to the Sun", which is derived from the Latin word sol, meaning Sun. The Sun is the dominant gravitational member of the Solar System, and its planetary system is maintained in a relatively stable, slowly evolving state by following isolated, gravitationally bound orbits around the Sun.
product-demo-collab-chat.TEXT_ORBITS_1: The planets and other large objects in orbit around the Sun lie near the plane of Earth's orbit, known as the ecliptic. Smaller icy objects such as comets frequently orbit at significantly greater angles to this plane. Most of the planets in the Solar System have secondary systems of their own, being orbited by natural satellites called moons. Many of the largest natural satellites are in synchronous rotation, with one face permanently turned toward their parent. The four giant planets have planetary rings, thin bands of tiny particles that orbit them in unison.
product-demo-collab-chat.TEXT_ORBITS_2: As a result of the formation of the Solar System, planets and most other objects orbit the Sun in the same direction that the Sun is rotating. That is, counter-clockwise, as viewed from above Earth's north pole. There are exceptions, such as Halley's Comet. Most of the larger moons orbit their planets in prograde direction, matching the planetary rotation; Neptune's moon Triton is the largest to orbit in the opposite, retrograde manner. Most larger objects rotate around their own axes in the prograde direction relative to their orbit, though the rotation of Venus is retrograde.
product-demo-collab-chat.TEXT_ORBITS_3: To a good first approximation, Kepler's laws of planetary motion describe the orbits of objects about the Sun. These laws stipulate that each object travels along an ellipse with the Sun at one focus, which causes the body's distance from the Sun to vary over the course of its year. A body's closest approach to the Sun is called its perihelion, whereas its most distant point from the Sun is called its aphelion.: 9-6  The orbits of the planets are nearly circular, but many comets, asteroids, and Kuiper belt objects follow highly elliptical orbits. Kepler's laws only account for the influence of the Sun's gravity upon an orbiting body, not the gravitational pulls of different bodies upon each other. On a human time scale, these additional perturbations can be accounted for using numerical models,: 9-6  but the planetary system can change chaotically over billions of years.
product-demo-collab-chat.TEXT_ORBITS_4: The angular momentum of the Solar System is a measure of the total amount of orbital and rotational momentum possessed by all its moving components. Although the Sun dominates the system by mass, it accounts for only about 2% of the angular momentum. The planets, dominated by Jupiter, account for most of the rest of the angular momentum due to the combination of their mass, orbit, and distance from the Sun, with a possibly significant contribution from comets.
product-demo-collab-chat.TEXT_COMPOSITION_1: The overall structure of the charted regions of the Solar System consists of the Sun, four smaller inner planets surrounded by a belt of mostly rocky asteroids, and four giant planets surrounded by the Kuiper belt of mostly icy objects. Astronomers sometimes informally divide this structure into separate regions. The inner Solar System includes the four terrestrial planets and the asteroid belt. The outer Solar System is beyond the asteroids, including the four giant planets. Since the discovery of the Kuiper belt, the outermost parts of the Solar System are considered a distinct region consisting of the objects beyond Neptune.
product-demo-collab-chat.TEXT_COMPOSITION_2: The principal component of the Solar System is the Sun, a low-mass star that contains 99.86% of the system's known mass and dominates it gravitationally. The Sun's four largest orbiting bodies, the giant planets, account for 99% of the remaining mass, with Jupiter and Saturn together comprising more than 90%. The remaining objects of the Solar System (including the four terrestrial planets, the dwarf planets, moons, asteroids, and comets) together comprise less than 0.002% of the Solar System's total mass.
product-demo-collab-chat.TEXT_COMPOSITION_3: The Sun is composed of roughly 98% hydrogen and helium, as are Jupiter and Saturn. A composition gradient exists in the Solar System, created by heat and light pressure from the early Sun; those objects closer to the Sun, which are more affected by heat and light pressure, are composed of elements with high melting points. Objects farther from the Sun are composed largely of materials with lower melting points. The boundary in the Solar System beyond which those volatile substances could coalesce is known as the frost line, and it lies at roughly five times the Earth's distance from the Sun.
product-demo-collab-chat.TEXT_COMPOSITION_4: The objects of the inner Solar System are composed mostly of rocky materials, such as silicates, iron or nickel. Jupiter and Saturn are composed mainly of gases with extremely low melting points and high vapour pressure, such as hydrogen, helium, and neon. Ices, like water, methane, ammonia, hydrogen sulfide, and carbon dioxide, have melting points up to a few hundred kelvins. They can be found as ices, liquids, or gases in various places in the Solar System. Icy substances comprise the majority of the satellites of the giant planets, as well as most of Uranus and Neptune (the so-called "ice giants") and the numerous small objects that lie beyond Neptune's orbit. Together, gases and ices are referred to as volatiles.

site-starter-packages.STARTER_ARTICLE_1_SUBTITLE: A beginner-friendly guide to tools and techniques.
site-starter-packages.STARTER_ARTICLE_2_SUBTITLE: Understanding color relationships for better compositions.
site-starter-packages.STARTER_ARTICLE_3_SUBTITLE: Tips for showcasing your best work online.
site-starter-packages.STARTER_HERO_SUBTITLE: Explore tutorials, resources, and inspiration for your creative journey.

site-starter-packages.STARTER_MEMBER_PORTAL_SUBTITLE: Manage your membership and account settings.
site-starter-packages.STARTER_ARTICLE_1_CONTENT:
Digital art opens up a world of creative possibilities. Whether you're working with a drawing tablet, an iPad, or even a mouse, modern tools make it easier than ever to bring your ideas to life. The key is to start simple and build your skills over time.

Begin by familiarizing yourself with your chosen software. Learn the basic brush tools, layers, and color pickers. Don't worry about creating a masterpiece right away — focus on getting comfortable with the interface and experimenting freely.

As you grow more confident, explore techniques like blending, masking, and working with references. The digital medium is forgiving — you can always undo, adjust, and iterate until your work feels right.
site-starter-packages.STARTER_ARTICLE_2_CONTENT:
Color theory is the foundation of effective visual communication. Understanding how colors interact helps you create compositions that feel harmonious, energetic, or dramatic — depending on your intent.

Start with the color wheel: primary, secondary, and tertiary colors form the basis of all color relationships. Complementary colors (opposite on the wheel) create contrast and vibrancy, while analogous colors (adjacent on the wheel) produce a more unified and calming effect.

Beyond the wheel, consider value (lightness and darkness) and saturation (intensity). A strong grasp of these properties allows you to guide the viewer's eye, set mood, and add depth to your artwork.
site-starter-packages.STARTER_ARTICLE_3_CONTENT:
Your portfolio is your first impression. It should showcase not just your best work, but also your range, process, and unique perspective as a creator. Quality matters more than quantity — curate carefully.

Organize your portfolio around projects or themes rather than listing every piece chronologically. Include brief descriptions that explain the context, your goals, and what you learned. This gives viewers insight into how you think and work.

Keep your portfolio updated and easy to navigate. A clean layout, fast loading times, and mobile-friendly design all contribute to a professional presentation that helps you stand out.
site-starter-packages.STARTER_PAGE_TUTORIALS_HERO_SUBTITLE: Step-by-step guides to level up your skills.
site-starter-packages.STARTER_PAGE_ART_CAREER_HERO_SUBTITLE: Advice and insights for building a career in art.
site-starter-packages.STARTER_PAGE_ART_CAREER_CONTENT:
Building a career in art takes more than talent — it requires persistence, adaptability, and a willingness to put yourself out there. Whether you're freelancing, seeking gallery representation, or exploring digital opportunities, the creative landscape is full of possibilities.

Start by defining your niche and understanding your audience. What makes your work unique? Who is drawn to your style? Answering these questions helps you position yourself in a crowded market and connect with the right people.

Networking, continuous learning, and consistent output are the pillars of a sustainable art career. Share your work regularly, seek feedback, and don't be afraid to evolve your practice over time.
site-starter-packages.STARTER_PAGE_RESOURCES_CONTENT:
We've gathered a collection of tools and references to support your creative workflow. From brushes and templates to color palettes and anatomy guides, these resources are designed to save you time and spark inspiration.

Explore our recommended software, hardware, and learning platforms. Whether you're just starting out or looking to refine your process, you'll find something useful here.

Check back regularly — we update this page with new finds and community recommendations.
site-starter-packages.STARTER_PAGE_LIBRARY_HERO_SUBTITLE: Browse our full collection of content.
site-starter-packages.STARTER_PAGE_ABOUT_HERO_SUBTITLE: Learn more about who we are and what we do.
site-starter-packages.STARTER_PAGE_ABOUT_CONTENT:
We're a community of creators, learners, and makers passionate about art and design. Our mission is to provide high-quality tutorials, resources, and inspiration to help you grow as a creative professional.

Whether you're a beginner picking up your first brush or an experienced artist exploring new mediums, you'll find a welcoming space here. We believe that everyone has the potential to create something meaningful.

Have questions or ideas? We'd love to hear from you. Reach out through our contact page and let's connect.

site-starter-packages.STARTER_PAGE_CONTACT_CONTENT:
We'd love to hear from you! Whether you have a question, feedback, or just want to say hello, don't hesitate to reach out.

Email us at hello@example.com and we'll get back to you as soon as possible. You can also connect with us on social media for updates and community discussions.

wordpress-spam.META_DESCRIPTION: Eliminate WordPress comment spam with FastComments. AI-powered spam detection, trainable classifiers, bot blocking, and seamless WordPress plugin integration.
wordpress-spam.HERO_TITLE: Stop WordPress Comment Spam. For Good.
wordpress-spam.HERO_DESCRIPTION: FastComments replaces your broken WordPress comment system with military-grade spam protection, real-time moderation, and a lightning-fast commenting experience your visitors will love.
wordpress-spam.PAIN_POINTS_TITLE: WordPress Spam Is Out of Control
wordpress-spam.PAIN_POINTS_SUBTITLE: If any of this sounds familiar, you're not alone.
wordpress-spam.PAIN_POINT_BOTS_DESCRIPTION: Automated bots hammer wp-comments-post.php and the REST API around the clock, filling your database with junk and slowing your site.
wordpress-spam.PAIN_POINT_MODERATION_DESCRIPTION: Hours spent reviewing, deleting, and banning spammers that keep coming back under new IPs and usernames.
wordpress-spam.PAIN_POINT_AKISMET_DESCRIPTION: Akismet catches some spam but lets sophisticated attacks through, still charges per-site, and does nothing to stop bots at the endpoint level.
wordpress-spam.ANTI_SPAM_SUBTITLE: Multiple layers of protection that work together to stop spam before it reaches your site.
wordpress-spam.ANTI_SPAM_BAYES_DESCRIPTION: Shared global model plus your own isolated classifier that learns from your moderation actions. Gets smarter every day.
wordpress-spam.ANTI_SPAM_AI_DESCRIPTION: Enable AI-powered content analysis to catch sophisticated spam that rule-based systems miss. Entirely optional — if you prefer not to share comment data with third-party providers, the built-in classifiers have you covered.
wordpress-spam.ANTI_SPAM_TRUST_DESCRIPTION: Automatically scores commenters based on behavior history. Trusted users post freely while new accounts face higher scrutiny.
wordpress-spam.ANTI_SPAM_REPEAT_DESCRIPTION: Detects and blocks duplicate or near-duplicate comments across your site, stopping copy-paste spam campaigns instantly.
wordpress-spam.ANTI_SPAM_PROFANITY_DESCRIPTION: Configurable word lists that automatically flag or block comments containing profanity, slurs, or custom banned terms.
wordpress-spam.ANTI_SPAM_BOT_DESCRIPTION: Bots targeting wp-comments-post.php and the WordPress REST API hit a dead end. Comments flow through FastComments' protected infrastructure instead.
wordpress-spam.ANTI_SPAM_UNVERIFIED_DESCRIPTION: Require email verification before comments appear. Unverified comments are automatically cleaned up, stopping throwaway-account spam.
wordpress-spam.ANTI_SPAM_AUDIT_DESCRIPTION: Full audit trail for every comment action. See exactly why a comment was flagged, who approved it, and track patterns over time.
wordpress-spam.WP_FEATURES_SUBTITLE: Deep WordPress integration that makes switching painless and adds capabilities you didn't know you needed.
wordpress-spam.WP_FEATURE_MIGRATION_DESCRIPTION: Import all your existing WordPress comments, including nested threads, author info, and timestamps. Nothing gets left behind.
wordpress-spam.WP_FEATURE_SYNC_DESCRIPTION: Comments sync back to your WordPress database daily. Your data stays yours, and SEO value is preserved.
wordpress-spam.WP_FEATURE_WOOCOMMERCE_DESCRIPTION: Product reviews and comment threads on WooCommerce pages work out of the box with full spam protection.
wordpress-spam.WP_FEATURE_SSO_DESCRIPTION: Logged-in WordPress users are automatically authenticated in FastComments. No double login, no friction.
wordpress-spam.WP_FEATURE_ZERO_DOWNTIME_DESCRIPTION: Install the plugin, enter your API key, and comments switch over instantly. No theme editing, no code changes.
wordpress-spam.WP_FEATURE_MULTISITE_DESCRIPTION: Run FastComments across your entire WordPress multi-site network with a single account and centralized moderation.
wordpress-spam.HOW_IT_WORKS_SUBTITLE: Three steps between you and spam-free comments.
wordpress-spam.HOW_IT_WORKS_STEP_1_DESCRIPTION: Search for "FastComments" in the WordPress plugin directory, install, and activate. Enter your API key in settings.
wordpress-spam.HOW_IT_WORKS_STEP_2_DESCRIPTION: One click imports all existing comments. The plugin handles threading, authors, and metadata automatically.
wordpress-spam.HOW_IT_WORKS_STEP_3_DESCRIPTION: Spam protection kicks in immediately. Watch your moderation queue go from overflowing to nearly empty.
wordpress-spam.FAQ_WP_SPAM_MIGRATE: Can I migrate my existing WordPress comments?
wordpress-spam.FAQ_WP_SPAM_MIGRATE_ANSWER: Yes. The FastComments WordPress plugin includes a one-click import that brings over all your existing comments, including nested threads, author information, and timestamps. The migration typically completes in under a minute for most sites.
wordpress-spam.FAQ_WP_SPAM_AKISMET: How does FastComments compare to Akismet?
wordpress-spam.FAQ_WP_SPAM_AKISMET_ANSWER: Akismet is a spam filter that sits on top of the default WordPress comment system. FastComments replaces the entire comment system with a purpose-built platform that includes multiple layers of spam protection (AI classifiers, trust scoring, bot blocking, profanity filters), plus features like real-time commenting, SSO, and detailed moderation tools. It's a complete solution, not just a filter.
wordpress-spam.FAQ_WP_SPAM_SEO_ANSWER: No. FastComments syncs comments back to your WordPress database daily, so search engines continue to index your comment content. Comments are also rendered in a way that is accessible to crawlers.
wordpress-spam.FAQ_WP_SPAM_WOOCOMMERCE_ANSWER: Yes. FastComments fully supports WooCommerce product reviews and comment threads. Spam protection applies to all comment types across your store.
wordpress-spam.FAQ_WP_SPAM_MULTISITE: Can I use it on a WordPress multi-site network?
wordpress-spam.FAQ_WP_SPAM_MULTISITE_ANSWER: Yes. Since WordPress uses numeric page IDs, you should create a separate tenant in your FastComments account for each site to keep comments separated. Moderation is centralized across all tenants, and each site gets full spam protection.
wordpress-spam.FAQ_WP_SPAM_SPEED: Will FastComments slow down my site?
wordpress-spam.FAQ_WP_SPAM_SPEED_ANSWER: No. FastComments loads asynchronously and is served from a global CDN. It's typically faster than the default WordPress comment system because it offloads comment rendering and spam processing from your server.
wordpress-spam.FINAL_CTA_DESCRIPTION: Join thousands of WordPress site owners who switched to FastComments and never looked back.

how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.PAGE_TITLE: How to Add Comments to a Website - FastComments
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.META_DESCRIPTION: Learn how to add comments to your website in minutes. FastComments provides a fast, lightweight commenting system that works with any platform - WordPress, React, Vue, Angular, and more.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.HERO_DESCRIPTION: Add a fast, lightweight comment section to any website in under 5 minutes for <%= startingPrice %>/mo without injecting ads to your site. No complex setup required. Fully customizable with CSS, with built-in spam protection.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.STEP_1_DESCRIPTION: Choose your framework below and copy the code snippet. The VanillaJS option works on any website with no build system required. For React, Vue, or Angular, install the npm package first.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.STEP_2_DESCRIPTION: Paste the snippet into your webpage where you want comments to appear. FastComments automatically creates a separate comment thread for each page based on the URL. If your platform supports HTML embed codes (like WordPress, Squarespace, or Webflow), just paste the VanillaJS snippet into an HTML block.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.STEP_2_DOCS_LINK: View full documentation for all frameworks
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.STEP_3_DESCRIPTION: Make it yours. FastComments supports custom CSS, dark mode, anonymous commenting, comment moderation, and much more. All configuration is available from your dashboard.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.STEP_4_DESCRIPTION: Sign up for a free trial to get your own tenant ID, then swap it into the snippet above. No credit card required.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.PLATFORMS_TITLE: No Code Required For Some Integrations
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.PLATFORMS_DESCRIPTION: FastComments integrates with all major platforms and frameworks. Click any platform for a step-by-step installation guide.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.WHY_FC_LIVE_DESC: Comments appear in real time with no page reload. Built-in live chat mode available.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.WHY_FC_FAST_DESC: <%= widgetSize %> gzipped. No impact on your page load speed or Core Web Vitals.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.WHY_FC_PRIVACY_DESC: No tracking cookies. No third-party analytics. Your visitors stay private.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.WHY_FC_DARK_DESC: Built-in dark mode support that respects your site's theme.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.WHY_FC_LANGUAGES_DESC: Fully localized in over <%= localeCount %> languages. Automatically matches your visitor's locale.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.WHY_FC_SSO_DESC: Integrate with your existing user system via secure SSO. SAML supported.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.BENEFITS_TITLE: Why Add Comments to Your Website?
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.BENEFITS_DESCRIPTION: Adding a comment section is one of the simplest and most effective ways to transform a static website into an interactive community. Here's why thousands of website owners add comments to their pages.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.BENEFIT_ENGAGEMENT_DESC: Visitors who leave comments stay on your site longer and return more often. A comment section turns passive readers into active participants, increasing page views and session duration.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.BENEFIT_SEO_DESC: Every comment adds fresh, keyword-rich content to your pages. Search engines favor pages with active discussions because they signal relevance and freshness, helping you rank higher for long-tail keywords.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.BENEFIT_COMMUNITY_DESC: Comments create a space for your audience to connect with you and each other. Over time, this builds a loyal community of brand advocates who share your content and bring in new visitors.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.BENEFIT_FEEDBACK_DESC: Your readers are a direct source of insights. Comments surface bug reports, content ideas, feature requests, and questions you might never have thought to ask in a survey.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.BENEFIT_SOCIAL_PROOF_DESC: An active comment section signals to new visitors that your content is worth reading and your site is trustworthy. Pages with visible engagement convert better than those without.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.FAQ_FREE_Q: Is it free to add comments to my website?
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.FAQ_FREE_A: FastComments offers a free 30-day trial with full access to all features. After the trial, paid plans start at <%= startingPrice %>/month. There are no per-comment or per-pageview fees, so your costs stay predictable as your site grows.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.FAQ_CODING_A: No. Adding FastComments to most platforms takes just a copy-paste of a small code snippet. If you use WordPress, Squarespace, Webflow, or Wix, you can embed it with their built-in HTML block — no coding knowledge required.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.FAQ_SPEED_Q: Will adding comments slow down my website?
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.FAQ_SPEED_A: FastComments is <%= widgetSize %> gzipped and loads asynchronously, so it does not block your page from rendering. It has no measurable impact on Core Web Vitals or Lighthouse scores.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.FAQ_MODERATION_Q: Can I moderate comments before they appear?
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.FAQ_MODERATION_A: Yes. FastComments includes built-in moderation tools, including pre-moderation (approve before publishing), keyword filters, spam detection, and the ability to ban users. You can moderate from the dashboard or via email notifications.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.FAQ_MIGRATION_Q: Can I migrate from Disqus or another comment system?
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.FAQ_MIGRATION_A: Yes. FastComments supports one-click import from Disqus, WordPress, Commento, and other platforms. Your existing comments, usernames, and timestamps are preserved during migration.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.FAQ_WORDPRESS_A: Yes. FastComments has a dedicated WordPress plugin that installs in under a minute in many cases. It automatically replaces the default WordPress comment form and imports your existing comments.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.FAQ_ANONYMOUS_Q: Can visitors comment without creating an account?
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.FAQ_ANONYMOUS_A: Yes. FastComments supports anonymous and guest commenting out of the box. Visitors can leave comments with just a name — no sign-up or email required. You can also enable SSO to let users comment with their existing account on your site.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.FAQ_GDPR_A: Yes. FastComments does not use tracking cookies or third-party analytics. All data is stored securely, and users can request data export or deletion. FastComments is fully GDPR and CCPA compliant.
how-to-add-comments-to-a-website.CTA_DESCRIPTION: Get started with a free trial. No credit card required.

laravel.FAQ_LARAVEL_SSO: How does SSO work with Laravel Auth?
laravel.FAQ_LARAVEL_SSO_ANSWER: When Secure SSO is enabled, the package reads the authenticated user from Laravel Auth and generates an HMAC-signed token on the server side. This creates or updates the user's FastComments account automatically with their name, email, and avatar. Users are signed in seamlessly without any extra registration.

laravel.FAQ_LARAVEL_API: Can I access the FastComments API from Laravel?
laravel.FAQ_LARAVEL_API_ANSWER: Yes. The package provides a FastComments Facade and supports dependency injection. You can use it to programmatically create, update, or delete comments, manage users, fetch analytics, and more from your controllers or jobs.

webinars.PHASE_BEFORE_SSO_DESC: Connect your identity provider via SSO or SAML so attendees use their existing accounts on your site. Or allow anonymous guest posting with just a display name - no signup friction.
webinars.LIFECYCLE_SUBTITLE: Most platforms make you choose between their chat and their ecosystem. FastComments is a standalone widget you embed on your own page - with full control at every stage of the event.
webinars.PHASE_BEFORE_RULES_DESC: Define keyword blocklists, enable ML-based spam detection, and set rate limits before the event starts. When the webinar goes live, moderation is already running.
webinars.PHASE_BEFORE_BRANDING_DESC: Inject custom CSS to match your site. Change colors, fonts, input styles, and avatar shapes. White-label removes the FastComments name entirely - it looks like part of your product.

webinars.PHASE_DURING_CHAT_DESC: Messages deliver in under one second worldwide through edge nodes on multiple continents. WebSocket-based pub/sub handles 100,000+ concurrent connections without degradation.
webinars.PHASE_DURING_QA_DESC: Attendees upvote questions they want answered. Moderators pin top questions and mark them answered. The audience decides what gets attention, not just who types fastest.
webinars.PHASE_DURING_MOD_DESC: One-click approve, hide, or ban. Bulk-select messages during high-volume moments. Assign multiple moderators so no one person has to monitor the entire chat alone.
webinars.PHASE_DURING_PIN_DESC: Pin announcements, key links, or top questions so they stay visible at the top of the chat as new messages scroll past.

webinars.PHASE_AFTER_PERSIST_DESC: Chat and Q&A data persists on your page permanently. Viewers watching the recording see the original discussion right where it happened. Nothing disappears when the stream ends.

webinars.COMPLIANCE_PRIVACY_DESC: GDPR compliant. No tracking cookies. No third-party ad scripts. Full data export and deletion on request. Your audience's data is not monetized.

webinars.DIFF_SCALE_DESC: No redirects to external platforms. Attendees watch, chat, and ask questions on your domain. You keep the traffic, the engagement, and the SEO value.

webinars.FAQ_WEBINARS_SCALE: How does FastComments handle 100,000+ concurrent viewers?
webinars.FAQ_WEBINARS_GUEST_ACCESS: Can attendees chat without creating an account?
webinars.FAQ_WEBINARS_MODERATION: How do I moderate chat during a live webinar?
webinars.FAQ_WEBINARS_GUEST_ACCESS_ANSWER: Yes. You have three identity modes. Anonymous guest posting lets attendees chat with no signup at all. Named guest posting asks for a display name but no email or password. Authenticated access via SSO ties chat participation to your existing user accounts. You configure which mode to use per page or per event.
webinars.FAQ_WEBINARS_SCALE_ANSWER: FastComments uses WebSocket-based pub/sub messaging with edge nodes on multiple continents. Messages are broadcast in real time with no polling. For rooms above 10,000 concurrent users, the system automatically adapts its delivery method to maintain sub-second latency. For rooms above 100,000, it shifts to an optimized polling mode. This happens transparently - attendees see no change in performance.
webinars.FAQ_WEBINARS_QA_VOTING_ANSWER: Yes. The voting system lets attendees upvote questions, surfacing the ones most people want answered. Moderators can pin questions to the top of the feed and post threaded replies. Pinned and top-voted questions stay visible even as new messages arrive, so your presenter can address what matters most to the audience.
webinars.FAQ_WEBINARS_PLATFORMS: What video players and platforms does FastComments work with?
webinars.FAQ_WEBINARS_MODERATION_ANSWER: Automated moderation runs before any message reaches the audience: keyword blocklists catch known bad words, and an ML spam classifier flags suspicious content. For manual moderation, your team can approve, hide, or ban users with one click. You can assign multiple moderators to share the workload, each with configurable permissions. Rate limiting prevents any single user from flooding the chat.
webinars.FAQ_WEBINARS_QA_VOTING: Can attendees upvote questions during the webinar?
webinars.FAQ_WEBINARS_AFTER_EVENT: What happens to the chat after the webinar ends?
webinars.FAQ_WEBINARS_PLATFORMS_ANSWER: FastComments is a JavaScript widget that runs on your webpage. It embeds alongside any video player: YouTube embeds, Vimeo embeds, Wistia, JW Player, HTML5 video, or any custom player. It also works with React, Vue, Angular, WordPress, and LMS platforms like Canvas. As long as the page can load a script tag, FastComments works.
webinars.FAQ_WEBINARS_AFTER_EVENT_ANSWER: Comments and Q&A data persist permanently on your page. When you replace the live stream with a recording, the original chat remains visible next to it. Viewers watching the replay can read all the questions and answers from the live session. If you use a new URL for each webinar, each event gets a fresh comment thread automatically. If you reuse the same URL, you can bulk delete the previous comments to start clean. You can also export everything as CSV or JSON, or push data to external tools via webhooks and Zapier.

webinars.FAQ_WEBINARS_PRICING_ANSWER: FastComments bills based on page loads and comment volume, not per viewer. A webinar with 50,000 attendees costs the same as one with 500 if the page load volume is within your plan. There are no per-seat charges for participants. news-sites.PAGE_TITLE: Live Commenting for News Sites | Real-Time Reader Engagement | FastComments
news-sites.META_DESCRIPTION: Add live commenting to your news site in minutes. FastComments handles millions of comments, traffic spikes, and moderation at scale, with a 30kb footprint that won't slow your pages. Trusted by <%- Number(Math.floor(usageStats.tenantCount / 100) * 100).toLocaleString() %>+ organizations.
news-sites.PROBLEM_P1: Most commenting systems were built for blogs, not newsrooms. They load slowly, drag down page performance, and treat a local city council story the same as a national election thread drawing thousands of simultaneous readers. The result is a comments section that either feels dead or collapses under its own weight, neither of which serves your audience or your editorial mission.
news-sites.MODERATION_TITLE: Moderation Tools Designed for Newsroom Volume
news-sites.WHY_FC_TITLE: A Commenting System Built for the Speed of News
news-sites.PROBLEM_P3: What news readers actually want is straightforward: they want to see comments appear in real time as a story develops, they want conversations that are moderated well enough to be worth reading, and they want to participate without surrendering their data to an advertising network. They want a comments section that respects both the story and the people reading it.
news-sites.WHY_FC_P2: During breaking news and major events like election nights, court rulings, and live sports, your traffic doesn't scale linearly, it spikes. FastComments handles <%- Number(usageStats.pageLoadCount).toLocaleString() %>+ page loads per year across its client base and supports millions of active comments without degradation. The infrastructure is built to absorb sudden, massive surges in concurrent readers and commenters. Your comments section stays responsive when it matters most.
news-sites.WHY_FC_P3: Performance is not a secondary consideration. The entire FastComments widget ships at roughly 30 kilobytes, a fraction of what systems like Disqus load onto your pages. That difference is significant for news sites, where every kilobyte affects page load time, Core Web Vitals scores, and ultimately your position in search results. Faster pages mean better SEO, lower bounce rates, and more ad impressions. A lightweight commenting system for publishers is not a luxury. It is a competitive advantage.
news-sites.PROBLEM_P2: The cost of getting it wrong is measurable. Slow-loading comment widgets hurt Core Web Vitals, which directly impacts your search rankings and ad revenue. Toxic or spam-filled threads erode reader trust and create legal and reputational risk. Heavy third-party scripts inject trackers that conflict with your privacy obligations and undermine the editorial independence your readers expect. And every reader who abandons your comments section is a reader who takes their engagement, and their loyalty, to social media instead.
news-sites.WHY_FC_P1: FastComments was engineered for exactly the conditions news sites face daily. Comments appear instantly for every reader on the page, with no reload, no polling delay, and no stale threads. When a story breaks and your audience surges to weigh in, the conversation keeps pace with events in real time. This is not a bolt-on feature. Live commenting is the foundation of how FastComments works.
news-sites.PROBLEM_TITLE: Commenting on News Sites Is Broken. Readers Know It.
news-sites.WHY_FC_P4: Integration is built for newsroom workflows. SSO lets your subscribers comment under their existing accounts. Webhooks push comment data into your CMS, analytics platforms, or moderation dashboards. Support for 14 languages with automatic detection means your international readership participates without friction. Whether you run a single metro daily or a network of publications across markets, FastComments fits the architecture you already have.
news-sites.SCALE_TITLE: Performance at the Scale News Demands
news-sites.PRIVACY_TITLE: Privacy That Matches Your Editorial Standards
news-sites.MODERATION_P1: News site moderation operates under constraints that most platforms never consider. A political story can generate hundreds of comments in minutes, a significant share of which may be inflammatory, off-topic, or outright spam. You need moderation that works at that velocity without requiring a staff of twenty people watching threads around the clock. A slow or clumsy moderation system does not just cost time. It lets toxic content sit in front of your readers and your advertisers.
news-sites.PRIVACY_P2: For news organizations, this is not merely a compliance checkbox. Your credibility depends on the trust your readers place in you. When a commenting system harvests user data or injects trackers, it creates a conflict between your editorial mission and your technology stack. Readers and regulators notice. FastComments removes that conflict entirely. Your comments section is a reader engagement tool, nothing more, and that clarity strengthens the relationship between your publication and your audience.
news-sites.PRIVACY_P1: FastComments is fully GDPR compliant and does not track, profile, or sell your readers' data. There are no hidden advertising pixels. No behavioral fingerprinting. No third-party data brokers riding on your comment widget. Your readers interact with your content, not with a surveillance layer disguised as engagement software. Anonymous commenting is available for stories where source protection or reader safety matters.
news-sites.SCALE_P1: FastComments processes over <%- Number(usageStats.pageLoadCount).toLocaleString() %> page loads per year and supports millions of comments across its client base of more than <%- Number(Math.floor(usageStats.tenantCount / 100) * 100).toLocaleString() %> organizations. The infrastructure is purpose-built for high-concurrency environments where thousands of readers load the same story simultaneously. Response times remain consistent whether a thread has ten comments or ten thousand.
news-sites.MODERATION_P2: FastComments includes a machine learning spam classifier that catches automated spam and coordinated abuse before it reaches your audience. Beyond automated filtering, the moderation interface supports bulk actions like approving, rejecting, or flagging dozens of comments in seconds. Moderation groups let you assign different teams to different sections or topics. Your politics desk can moderate their threads independently from your sports editors, each with their own rules and escalation paths.
news-sites.MIGRATION_TITLE: Migrate From Disqus or WordPress Comments in Minutes
news-sites.SCALE_P2: Traffic spikes are not an edge case for news sites. They are the normal operating condition during any significant story. FastComments does not throttle, queue, or degrade during surges. There are no per-pageview pricing traps that penalize you for having a successful story. When your audience grows, your commenting system should keep up without sending you an overage invoice. With both fixed and flexible pricing plans, your costs stay predictable even when your traffic doesn't.
news-sites.MODERATION_P3: The goal is civil discourse without silence. Heavy-handed moderation kills conversation. Absent moderation breeds toxicity. FastComments gives your team the precision tools to enforce community standards quickly while keeping the productive, substantive reader conversations that build audience loyalty and distinguish your publication from the noise of social media.
news-sites.MIGRATION_P2: There is no extended parallel-run period and no engineering project required. The typical migration takes minutes, not weeks. Your development team adds a lightweight script tag, configures your preferences, and your comments section is live with full history preserved.
news-sites.COMMUNITY_P1: A comments section is the starting point, not the destination. FastComments includes awards and badges that recognize your most thoughtful contributors, reactions beyond simple upvotes, and built-in surveys that let you gauge reader sentiment on the issues you cover. Direct messaging between users lets conversations continue beyond individual threads. These are the tools that turn one-time commenters into regular participants and regular participants into loyal subscribers.
news-sites.MIGRATION_P1: Switching commenting systems sounds disruptive. In practice, FastComments imports your existing comments from Disqus, WordPress, and other platforms with a straightforward migration tool. Your existing threads, usernames, and conversation history transfer intact. Readers return to find their past comments exactly where they left them, and the transition is seamless enough that most will not notice the change, only the improvement.
news-sites.COMMUNITY_P2: Reader engagement on news sites competes directly with social media for attention and habit formation. The publications that win that competition are the ones that give their audience a reason to come back to the source. Analytics built into FastComments show you which stories drive the most engagement, which commenters are most active, and how your community is growing over time.
news-sites.CTA_SUBTITLE: No page slowdowns, no privacy trade-offs, no scaling surprises. See what FastComments looks like on your site with a free trial, no credit card required.
news-sites.CTA_TITLE: Your Readers Are Already Talking. Give Them a Better Place to Do It.
news-sites.NEWSPACK_TITLE: FastComments Works With Newspack, Out of the Box
news-sites.NEWSPACK_COMPARE_CAPTION: Newspack default comments compared with FastComments
news-sites.NEWSPACK_P1: Newspack is built on WordPress, and so is the FastComments plugin. If you publish with Newspack, you do not switch platforms or rebuild anything. Install the FastComments WordPress plugin on your Newspack site, connect it in a few clicks, and live commenting is running in minutes. Your posts, your theme, and your editorial workflow stay exactly where they are.
news-sites.NEWSPACK_P3: You keep Newspack for everything it does well, publishing, membership, and your editorial operation, and FastComments takes over the conversation. It is fully GDPR compliant, it does not track or profile your readers, and it loads no advertising pixels onto your pages. The result is a comments section that matches the standards your newsroom already holds itself to, running on the platform you have already chosen.
news-sites.NEWSPACK_P2: Newspack ships with WordPress's native comments, and those comments carry every limitation WordPress brings with them. There are no real-time updates, so readers refresh the page to see new replies. The markup adds weight that drags down Core Web Vitals on article pages already heavy with ads and media. Spam protection is thin, and moderation means working through the wp-admin queue one comment at a time. On a breaking story drawing thousands of readers at once, that model does not hold up. FastComments replaces it with instant, live comments that appear as the conversation happens, at a footprint of roughly 30 kilobytes.
